title: whcw-1996-world
label: Adonis Mercury

won.source: Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as a five-time former WHCW World Champion, with individual reign dates not given.

lost.note: Mercury's own on-air account blames a contract dispute engineered by the promotion's president for costing him the title, rather than a match.

note: The promotion's own broadcast does not name a wrestler holding the title after Mercury; its status is not attested in this record.

title: whcw-1996-north-american
label: “Casanova” Chris Tyler

won.source: Reached the vacant title first during an unsanctioned construction-site brawl and had the win confirmed by the promotion's own president over the phone, on the same broadcast.

note: No stipulation had named a formal winner for the title inside the brawl itself; the promotion's own president ruled on it afterward.

title: whcw-1996-north-american
label: Kensai Akira

won.source: Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as a former WHCW North American Champion.

note: How and when the reign ended is not given; the title was vacant by the time of this broadcast.

won.source: Won the WHCW North American Tag Team Championship from the Sociopaths after revealing themselves from beneath a disguise.
Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as the reigning WHCW North American Tag Team Champions entering the card.

lost.source: Pinned by the returning Ultranationalists after a backstage beatdown left them battered before the bell.

lost.note: Commentary on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast states Speed Racer beat Dragon for the title, without giving a date.

title: whcw-1996-cruiserweight
label: Speed Racer

won.source: Won the title from Dragon, per the promotion's own commentary; the date of the win is not given.

note: Successfully defended the title against “Gimmickless” Gary Garvin at Rumble in the Bronx 2 with a top-rope Flatliner, in 9 minutes 56 seconds.

won.source: Won a five-man steel cage elimination match for the vacant title, outlasting Sennaga Cortez, the Inferno Kid, Guy LaChance and Hooligan.

title: whcw-1996-extreme
label: Doomsday

won.source: Referenced only in passing on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast, as the standard the new champion was compared against.

lost.note: Not attested in this record; the title was vacant by the time of this broadcast.

note: Commentary calls this new champion unlikely to 'live up to Doomsday's reign,' the only evidence for it in this record.
